mainEntity.name: How long after having composite bonding can it be reshaped?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding can technically be assessed and reshaped at any point after initial placement, though most dentists recommend waiting at least two to four weeks before requesting adjustments. This allows you time to fully adjust to the feel and appearance of the bonding in everyday situations. Minor adjustments to bite or surface smoothness are sometimes carried out at a follow-up appointment shortly after initial treatment. For more significant changes, it is sensible to discuss your concerns at a dedicated review appointment so your dentist can assess the bonding thoroughly and advise appropriately.

mainEntity.name: Will reshaping composite bonding damage my natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: When carried out by a qualified dentist, reshaping composite bonding should not damage the natural tooth beneath. Dentists use fine instruments calibrated to work on the composite layer rather than the underlying tooth structure. However, if composite bonding has become very thin over time, careful assessment is needed before further removal. This is one reason why professional evaluation before any reshaping work is so important — it ensures that your natural tooth structure is fully taken into account during the process.

Most patients find reshaping composite bonding to be a comfortable, straightforward procedure. Because the composite resin itself does not have nerve supply, reshaping it directly is unlikely to cause discomfort. However, if a significant amount of material is removed and the underlying dentine becomes closer to the surface, some temporary sensitivity can occasionally occur. Your dentist can advise you on this during your assessment and can take steps to minimise any discomfort if needed. Local anaesthetic is rarely required for straightforward reshaping appointments.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to have composite bonding reshaped in London?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of reshaping or adjusting composite bonding will vary depending on the complexity of the work involved, the number of teeth affected, and the dental practice you attend. Minor polishing or bite adjustments may sometimes be included within a post-treatment review, while more significant reshaping or additional composite application will typically incur a separate fee. A full breakdown of costs will be provided in a personalised treatment plan following your consultation appointment. It is worth discussing costs clearly with your dental practice before proceeding so that you can make a fully informed decision.

mainEntity.name: How many times can composite bonding be reshaped?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no fixed maximum number of times composite bonding can be reshaped, but each adjustment that involves removing material gradually reduces the total volume of composite on the tooth. Over time, if composite is repeatedly thinned, the options for further reshaping become more limited. This is why careful planning from the outset and good aftercare in the intervening period are both important. Your dentist will be able to assess the current condition of your bonding and advise how feasible further reshaping would be in your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: Can composite bonding be completely replaced if reshaping is not sufficient?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If reshaping is not sufficient to achieve the desired result — or if the existing bonding has worn, stained, or debonded to a significant degree — composite bonding can be fully replaced. The existing material is carefully removed, the tooth surface is prepared, and fresh composite resin is applied. In some cases, where a more durable or long-lasting result is the goal, a dentist may also discuss alternative options such as porcelain veneers. The most appropriate choice will depend on your individual clinical situation and aesthetic goals, and should be discussed in full during a consultation.
